membership_logic_verifier.evidence: the check counts users 1, 3 and 5 in group 19 and expects 2, so it also passes when the inactive Thomas Green (user 1, active = 0 in the seed) is added in place of an active member; the request asks for active users only, so the members are users 3 and 5, each tested separately. The check's description names skill 5 (Exit Interviews), but the IT skill is skill 13, which all three L1 members hold; the query does not use the skill

notes:
disagreement: value: the membership rows: one pass counts users 3 and 5 in group 19 in one requirement expecting 2, the other gives each user its own requirement expecting 1; kept one per user, the tighter form (logged in those requirements).
disagreement: value: the cases' opened_by: one pass tests 39, the other leaves it untested because every seed case sets opened_by equal to opened_for; kept 39 because policy 3.1 makes opened_by the requester, the acting user (logged in both case requirements).
The two passes otherwise agree on every requirement, id, cell and disposition (two checks kept, the membership check repaired); their texts and assumptions differ in wording only.
The request says 'a specific expert' but then 'add them'; the seed yields two qualifying users (3 and 5), matching the benchmark's expected 2, so both are required.
The two case requirements carry the benchmark's single set check, adding each employee's account number from the request.
assigned_to is not tested: policy 3.2 asks for an active assignee from the assignment group, but the request names only the group and the system's assignment rule runs on creation (if set, it should be user 3 or 5).
The policy's short-description template ends with a full stop; the request gives the exact text without one, and that text is required, as the benchmark does.
The acting user Karen Watkins holds the admin role, and the policy says administrators must not perform routine HR case work; the request frames the cases as part of setting up an emergency workflow and the benchmark expects them, so they are required, though a reviewer may judge that the agent should have declined that step.
The source and org_id of the new rows are not fixed by the request or policy and are not tested.
